about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Nothing new on supply or demand over the Thanksgiving break; the holiday-delayed export sales are already in the desk model. Friday's short session leaves old-crop Mar to trade outside markets, which lean supportive with crude firmer and a broad commodity bid.
events: Mar last ~82.0 after Tuesday's push through 82.7 resistance (ICE)
Crude up ~1.7% on Gulf supply disruptions (Reuters, OilPrice)
Broad metals and equity-index bid into Friday (Bloomberg, WSJ)

sugar.fundamental: The real's ~5% jump after Bradesco chairman Trabuco agreed to become finance minister lifts the dollar cost of Brazilian sugar and should slow mill forward pricing, which trims the near-term supply pressure from the Centre-South. Mar is through the 18.35/18.38 resistance; the fund long that was not flushed out remains the swing factor.
events: Trabuco agrees to take Brazil finance ministry; USD/BRL ~5.50 (-5.5%) and Bovespa +6% (Reuters, Yahoo Finance)

coffee.fundamental: A sharply stronger real reduces the incentive for Brazilian growers to sell, a modest prop for arabica; it does not change the deliverability picture, and ICE certified stocks/Antwerp flows remain the deciding input, with no new cert data over the holiday.
events: Real rallies ~5.5% on Trabuco finance-minister pick (Reuters, Yahoo Finance)
London robusta bounce off a three-year low earlier in the week (ICE Europe)
Vietnam harvest selling still weighs on robusta (Reuters)

cocoa.fundamental: No new Ivorian arrival or grind data over the US holiday, and ICCO has not yet published its November quarterly bulletin, so the balance read is unchanged: slow arrivals offer short-term support against rising ICE certified stocks.
events: Slow Ivorian arrivals kept NY near a one-month high into the holiday (Reuters, Barchart)
